newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Industry to tell Menem labor deal "no use at all".
newsitem.headline: Industry to tell Menem labor deal "no use at all".

text.p: Argentine industry chiefs will meet President Carlos Menem next Monday to complain about their exclusion from labor reform proposals the government has drawn up with trade unions, they said Friday.

The Group of Eight main industry chambers want to air their grievances about the "Act of Agreement" that the CGT labor federation and Peronist government drew up late last month behind businessmen's backs, and plan to send to Congress.

Carlos de la Vega, deputy chairman of the Argentine Chamber of Commerce, said after the Group of Eight met at the Buenos Aires Stock Exchange that they wanted to talk to Menem about "the suspension of negotiations with the CGT (labor federation), which to tell the truth never really began."
"It is clear that the CGT has not permitted at any moment the idea of sitting down to discuss the text already agreed on with the government," De la Vega told reporters.
The Argentine Industrial Union's chief Claudio Sebastiani said the agreement waters down Menem's original plans for far-reaching reforms of labor laws and "is no use at all."

The two-way pact, made after Menem's attempts to reform by decree were rejected by courts and the three-way talks with unions, government and business failed to get results, goes back on plans to scrap centralized pay talks and to swap redundancy payments for unemployment insurance schemes.
The Peronist government is under pressure to come up with measures to combat Argentina's 17.3 percent unemployment rate ahead of key mid-term elections in Congress in October.
The CGT meets Menem next Tuesday and CGT officials told Reuters Thursday that they did not want any more talks with the business lobbies, but wanted the debate moved to Congress.
One pro-union Peronist Congressman, Jose Luis Castillo, said Friday that if the government-union proposal went to Congress, it could be passed in a month.

But business leaders say the reforms worked out with the CGT will not create jobs. They are angry at the government, and especially Labor Ministero Armando Caro Figueroa, for leaving them out of the deal.
"We are convinced society wants jobs to be created, but we don't believe this agreement is the way to generate them," said the Chamber of Commerce chairman Carlos Di Fiori.

"We don't like the minister's attitude," said Enrique Crotto of the farmers' lobby. "We're disconcerted because the last time we took them our proposals, the minister told us the government would mediate an agreement, then told us they had come up with this agreement and it could not be negotiated."
